usedHookFrames: pre-suasion-ch01: The fee has not been named yet, but the first number in the room is already doing work.
pre-suasion-ch02: A red donor card works only after someone has just remembered being useful.
pre-suasion-ch03: The cracked tile gets every eye, while the warm cooler log sits quietly on the clipboard.
pre-suasion-ch04: One suitcase wedged sideways can look like the cause of every late bag in the airport.
pre-suasion-ch05: A black tray on a silver packing line stops hands faster than another warning memo.
pre-suasion-ch06: The blank field on the hawk card keeps every volunteer watching the carrier.
pre-suasion-ch07: A handoff checklist changes when it sits beside a family photo consent form.
pre-suasion-ch08: The same refund prompt changes when it appears at the first moment of confusion.
pre-suasion-ch09: The first screen on the triage tablet can ready shame before symptoms are even sorted.
pre-suasion-ch10: Twelve circled winter beds make scarcity cleaner than any deadline banner.
pre-suasion-ch11: The old postmark matters before the fragile letters ever leave the family table.
pre-suasion-ch12: The rule ballot lands differently after eight oars rise on the same count.
pre-suasion-ch13: The revenue line looks clean until someone writes the trust cost beside it.
pre-suasion-ch14: The attic ladder is still down when the insulation quote lands on the calendar.
usedCounterFrames: pre-suasion-ch01: A stronger request is often too late. The sharper move is to prepare receptivity before the request, while the listener can still meet the message without feeling pushed.

pre-suasion-ch02: The opening is not merely good timing. A privileged moment appears when a pre-question makes a relevant self-image active, so the request meets someone already standing in that identity.
pre-suasion-ch03: Attention does not just reveal importance. It can manufacture the feeling of importance, making one loud factor seem heavier than quieter evidence that matters more.
pre-suasion-ch04: The feature in the spotlight often feels causal because it is available, not because it explains the result. The better move is to follow evidence away from the focal object.
pre-suasion-ch05: An attractor is not a louder version of your message. Threat, difference, and goal relevance seize attention cleanly only when they belong to the decision itself.
pre-suasion-ch06: Held attention is not the same as suspense. A magnetizer works when self-relevance, unfinished information, or mystery keeps the mind with a question the message can truly answer.
pre-suasion-ch07: Positive feeling is too blunt. Association works when the target idea is linked to a favorable meaning the audience already respects, not when any pleasant cue is placed nearby.
pre-suasion-ch08: Persuasive place is not decoration. A setting carries traces that can lower resistance or distort judgment before the offer’s merits are weighed.
pre-suasion-ch09: Prepared concepts are not commands. They are temporary activations that help or distort depending on relevance, limits, and the corrective you place nearby.
pre-suasion-ch10: The six principles are not buttons to press in sequence. The smart move is to frontload the one principle that honestly fits the choice and leave the others alone.
pre-suasion-ch11: Unity is not friendliness. It is a We relationship made conscious through legitimate identity, family, or place before cooperation is requested.
pre-suasion-ch12: Shared activity is not unity unless the action creates real togetherness tied to the later ask. Icebreakers pass time; synchronized or collaborative work changes the relationship.
pre-suasion-ch13: Ethics is not a polish pass after the tactic works. The first decision is whether the attention plan deserves to exist at all.
pre-suasion-ch14: A yes created by attention is fragile. Post-suasion starts while the reason is still visible, turning the moment into a next action before it cools.
usedTryThisNowFrames: pre-suasion-ch01: Before your next ask, choose one honest cue the other person should encounter first: a number, object, question, or shared fact that makes the request easier to judge.
pre-suasion-ch02: Write the request you want to make, then add one pre-question that lets the person recall a real helpful, careful, or adventurous act before you ask.
pre-suasion-ch03: For one decision today, write the factor everyone is staring at. Then write the quiet factor that would matter if nobody had pointed a light at either one.
pre-suasion-ch04: Pick one problem on your desk. Write the visible symptom on the left, then write one hidden process that could have produced it on the right.
pre-suasion-ch05: Before sending one message, label its opening cue as threat, difference, or goal relevance. If none truthfully fits, open with plain context instead.
pre-suasion-ch06: Take one ignored request and turn it into a real unanswered question. Name what is unfinished, personal, or unknown, then answer it directly.
pre-suasion-ch07: Name one value your audience already defends. Then write the exact, truthful link between that value and the request you plan to make.
pre-suasion-ch08: Move one request to the place where the person already feels the problem clearly. Write the trace that place adds before you deliver it.
pre-suasion-ch09: Find one first cue in a form or script. Write what it readies, what it could distort, and the correction that should appear before the decision.
pre-suasion-ch10: Choose one request and circle one fitting principle: reciprocity, liking, authority, social proof, scarcity, or consistency. Delete cues for the rest.
pre-suasion-ch11: Before asking for help, write the real We that already exists. If the phrase sounds borrowed, flattering, or vague, do not use it.
pre-suasion-ch12: Before a cooperation request, design one thirty-second action people can do together that mirrors the support you need from them.
pre-suasion-ch13: Before improving one persuasive cue, write three lines: who benefits, who could be misled, and what trust cost would make the cue unacceptable.
pre-suasion-ch14: After the next fresh yes, schedule or perform one concrete follow-through while the object, reason, or evidence behind the yes is still in view.
usedQuizExplanationFrames: pre-suasion-ch01/q01: The screenshot prepares the ground for the price by making the problem visible. A warmer tone may help delivery, and delay may create suspicion, but neither changes what is salient before the fee.

pre-suasion-ch01/q02: The returned forms let the board see the failure before hearing the staffing request. More legal detail repeats the old route, and asking for trust tries to collect receptivity after resistance has formed.

pre-suasion-ch01/q03: The opening framed the call as something to escape quickly, so the later pledge had poor soil. A bigger anchor could be manipulative, and more story after the ask arrives too late.

pre-suasion-ch01/q04: The side-by-side tasting makes quality the first comparison, so the price has a truthful anchor. Ingredient inflation centers the chef’s problem, while a deadline pressures more than it prepares.

pre-suasion-ch01/q05: The anchor can change comparison, but the later complaint is evidence that the cue was not experienced as fair. Better humor will not fix a setup that leaves people feeling manipulated.

pre-suasion-ch01/q06: The cracked swing mount makes the need concrete before the fee appears, while the exact sheet keeps the cost visible. Asking for a vote before the total hides the choice instead of preparing it.
pre-suasion-ch01/q07: The correction keeps the focus on relevant receptivity, not charm. Luxury context is too narrow, and confidence plus timing turns the idea back into ordinary sales polish.

pre-suasion-ch01/q08: The marked bill creates prepared ground for joint problem-solving. It is not mere distraction, and neutrality matters less than the fact that both people act on the same shared cost first.

pre-suasion-ch01/q09: The pressure map truthfully prepares the price by showing the discomfort it addresses. Naming price first may sound clean but leaves the problem abstract, while banning visuals confuses fair context with manipulation.

pre-suasion-ch02/q01: The helper question creates the privileged moment by making a true self-image salient. Distraction would be weaker, and public pressure would corrupt the request rather than prepare it.
pre-suasion-ch02/q02: The brave-trip question wakes up adventurous identity while the advisory keeps the choice fair. The other options flatter or narrow attention by hiding the full decision.
pre-suasion-ch02/q03: The shelf question activates ownership, which is the relevant receptive state. Convenience and placement help, but they do not explain why the request lands as stewardship.

pre-suasion-ch02/q04: The bug question calls up careful critic identity, which fits a beta that needs testing. Shiny features and early access wake up novelty or status, not the job the product manager needs done.
pre-suasion-ch02/q05: If the question does not connect to a real memory, it becomes a costume. The map and neighbor memory keep the request tied to actual preparedness instead of invented warmth.
pre-suasion-ch02/q06: Guilt converts a receptive identity into pressure. The memory can prepare guardianship cleanly, but only if the later request stays voluntary and specific.

pre-suasion-ch02/q07: Broad identity prompts can become empty. A privileged moment needs a self-image tied to the real choice, such as preserving a gallery or supporting access, not just a flattering label.

pre-suasion-ch02/q08: The outage question activates prepared-neighbor identity, which fits alerts. Being first or tired of updates points toward status or irritation, neither as cleanly connected to the civic request.
pre-suasion-ch02/q09: Emotion alone is not enough. The receptive window is privileged because the right concern or self-image is salient at decision time, not because the room feels warm.

pre-suasion-ch03/q01: The log needs foreground attention because it carries the larger risk. The tile is visible, but visibility alone should not set the budget; splitting money dodges the importance question.

pre-suasion-ch03/q02: The due date deserves the first slot because it prevents the next fee. A brighter badge worsens the salience problem, and extra explanation arrives after attention has already been spent.
pre-suasion-ch03/q03: The nurse does not discard the rash; she prevents the vivid photo from crowding out a quieter symptom. The wrong answers either surrender to salience or overcorrect.

pre-suasion-ch03/q04: Reading the gap aloud gives the neglected evidence attention at the decision point. Paint may affect resale, but it should not swallow maintenance risk, and hiding the folder removes relevant weight.
pre-suasion-ch03/q05: The counts are better evidence for crowd risk, and pinning them over the email gives them needed salience. Anger and recency are attention cues, not proof of importance.
pre-suasion-ch03/q06: Reading the aid line first gives need proper decision weight before style creates a halo. Hiding essays removes relevant evidence, and equal need scores erase real differences.
pre-suasion-ch03/q07: The correction separates salience from importance. Ignoring discussion would throw away useful signals, while consensus can still be formed around a loud but minor cue.
pre-suasion-ch03/q08: Equalizing vividness tests whether attention is inflating one risk. Public ease and meeting order are salience conditions, not measures of actual importance.
pre-suasion-ch03/q09: The risk appears when vivid attention distorts scale. A concrete story can help, and placement before numbers is not automatically wrong if the broader evidence stays visible.
pre-suasion-ch04/q01: The wedged suitcase is focal, but timestamps and staffing records trace the causal chain. Photos show what people saw, not necessarily what produced the delay.
pre-suasion-ch04/q02: Hiding the focal flag tests whether a less visible pattern explains the spike. Permanent removal or quick blocking both let the most obvious cue drive causality too soon.
pre-suasion-ch04/q03: The leaves show damage, but the dry tube may explain it. The right move keeps the leaves as evidence while checking the hidden system that could have caused them.
pre-suasion-ch04/q04: Sequence tests causality. If listeners left before the joke, the focal memory cannot explain the drop, while comments and host feelings may only repeat what is most memorable.
pre-suasion-ch04/q05: The lot-matched inserts reveal a packing-pressure pattern outside the focal crack. Better photos and impressions only intensify attention to the visible damage.
pre-suasion-ch04/q06: The chart makes a plausible hidden process visible before donors lock onto neglect. Apology concedes too soon, and hiding the tank removes evidence rather than balancing it.

pre-suasion-ch04/q07: The correction keeps the useful clue while rejecting automatic causality. Crowds can notice real symptoms, and experts still need visible evidence, but attribution requires tracing.
pre-suasion-ch04/q08: The bus pattern could be causal even if it is less discussed. Staff complaints show salience; the records test whether the timing fits a hidden cause.
pre-suasion-ch04/q09: The timeout comparison tests a hidden causal path. Reversing or surveying only the visible color lets focality write the explanation before evidence does.
pre-suasion-ch05/q01: The stencil ties threat to the exact step commuters must change. The crash photo and vague warning attract fear, but they do not give precise guidance for the decision.
pre-suasion-ch05/q02: The black tray creates relevant difference at the point of action. A verbal reminder fades into routine, and music changes mood without marking the allergen risk.
pre-suasion-ch05/q03: The pace band connects salt to the runner’s own finish goal. Shouting may overplay threat, and hiding water manipulates access rather than guiding attention.
pre-suasion-ch05/q04: The bin ties the deadline to the caregiver’s active school-prep goal. Accuracy did not change, and distance is less important than the cue’s fit with the task.
pre-suasion-ch05/q05: The real chirp is both different and diagnostic. A theatrical siren or random tone captures attention without connecting to the equipment risk.
pre-suasion-ch05/q06: The seal marks the specific dangerous lot, so attention lands where action is needed. Looking official is secondary, and the cue supports the lot check rather than replacing it.
pre-suasion-ch05/q07: Threat cues should match real threat. A fake warning may win the open and lose trust, while size cannot make a mismatched attractor honest.
pre-suasion-ch05/q08: Difference attracts because it breaks a pattern. If every item is marked the same way, the cue no longer signals a real distinction.
pre-suasion-ch05/q09: The sticker fits the parent’s current school-readiness goal. The photo overuses threat, and the prize wheel attracts attention without connecting to the health choice.
pre-suasion-ch06/q01: The address holds attention because it changes the homeowner’s own situation. Formality is secondary, and the premium table still matters after the personal risk is clear.

pre-suasion-ch06/q02: The unresolved stair keeps attention on the problem the critique must solve. A finished rendering closes the loop too soon, and prettiness pulls attention away from the design issue.
pre-suasion-ch06/q03: The mystery is fair because the greeting note closes the open question. Game feel is not the point, and withholding all evidence would make prediction pointless.

pre-suasion-ch06/q04: The blank field should hold attention on the consequence of incomplete records. Filling it too fast closes the loop, while rescue photos add emotion without teaching the intake need.

pre-suasion-ch06/q05: The empty slot creates attention and the evidence card closes it. An unanswered dramatic question is unfair, and showing everything at once may fail to hold attention on the gap.
pre-suasion-ch06/q06: The real export task is a legitimate open loop; the fake bar is a trap. Cheerful design or hidden controls still manipulate held attention.
pre-suasion-ch06/q07: Curiosity is being borrowed without a matching answer. Length is not the issue, and a discount may be relevant, but it does not close the promised secret.
pre-suasion-ch06/q08: The specific molar makes the plan personally relevant to that family. The generic opener does not magnetize, and regret language uses pressure rather than relevance.
pre-suasion-ch06/q09: Mystery should hold attention for a real answer. Treating it as a universal style turns the cue into delay, and hiding data weakens judgment.
pre-suasion-ch07/q01: The form links handoff work to a value nurses already defend. Color and optionality miss the point: association changes meaning while the checklist still matters.
pre-suasion-ch07/q02: The farm label supplies a real favorable association. Design time is irrelevant, and making weight look larger would distort rather than connect.
pre-suasion-ch07/q03: Random nostalgia is a loose pleasant cue. The old stub works because it links renewal to a real memory and belonging the patron already has.
pre-suasion-ch07/q04: The client note connects the reset to professional trust. The breach warning may be threat, and the slogan is pleasant but too thin to carry meaning.
pre-suasion-ch07/q05: The attendance sheet links money to visible effort. It need not distract or shame; the clean version uses a value parents already saw.
pre-suasion-ch07/q06: The association fails if craft pride is borrowed for unrelated data capture. Placement in the box is not the issue; the truth of the link is.
pre-suasion-ch07/q07: Association needs a truthful link, not generic positivity. Pleasant feeling alone may float free from the actual relief need, and volume only increases the mismatch.
pre-suasion-ch07/q08: The note links the form to a patient benefit already relevant to care. Candy and beach photos may feel pleasant, but they do not make the form’s meaning clearer.
pre-suasion-ch07/q09: The correction preserves association while requiring fit. Good mood can matter, but loose positivity without a real link does not teach why the request belongs.
pre-suasion-ch08/q01: The document-check table carries a planning trace that fits the choice. The exit desk adds hurry, and the coffee poster is nearby but not tied to the decision.
pre-suasion-ch08/q02: Bedside placement lowers embarrassment and keeps the schedule visible. Louder checkout questions intensify the bad setting, and a later survey misses the teachable place.
pre-suasion-ch08/q03: The hallway’s trace changes reception before substance lands. Brighter paper or extra vocabulary does not address the defensive setting.
pre-suasion-ch08/q04: The service bay supplies the relevant repair trace. The booth risks making debt feel like a sales event, and pretending placement has no effect ignores the placement principle.
pre-suasion-ch08/q05: The storage room links the ask to preservation through place and trace. Stage volume and themed pastries decorate the appeal without moving it closer to the problem.
pre-suasion-ch08/q06: The quiz result is the psychological place where confusion becomes exit. Help belongs at the felt problem, not only where the site map stores policy.
pre-suasion-ch08/q07: The useful question links place to judgment. Scent and decoration may alter mood, but they do not prove the setting carries the right meaning.
pre-suasion-ch08/q08: The stair location carries the actual repair trace while the estimate keeps cost visible. Hidden ballots and mood music shape response without supporting fair judgment.
pre-suasion-ch08/q09: Placement may be creating resistance before words are weighed. More detail might help later, but first the message needs a fair geography.
pre-suasion-ch09/q01: The order may activate money anxiety before pain reporting. The point is not that coverage never matters, but that early activation can distort the next answer.
pre-suasion-ch09/q02: Reordering tests whether the early concept was contaminating fairness ratings. Deletion may lose useful information, and a warning alone may not change activation.
pre-suasion-ch09/q03: A neutral opener reduces shame activation before help appears. Repeating the balance may deepen the problem, while hiding it removes relevant information.
pre-suasion-ch09/q04: The correction keeps curiosity inside evidence limits. Removing curiosity wastes a useful magnetizer, and a larger button would intensify the same problem.
pre-suasion-ch09/q05: The issue is cue reach. The icon may ready caution beyond its intended scope; insulting diners or hiding all information misses the corrective test.
pre-suasion-ch09/q06: The neutral opener prevents broad resentment activation, and the preserve item corrects range. Cheerful images and instructions do not address the readied concept.
pre-suasion-ch09/q07: The answer keeps the mechanism and the limits together. The other choices deny the effect or exaggerate it into permanent control.
pre-suasion-ch09/q08: The early warning may activate suspicion beyond its proper target. The corrective is to test placement and scope, not dismiss ratings altogether.
pre-suasion-ch09/q09: The responsible plan pairs activation with an immediate corrective. Fear and withholding both exploit the opened loop rather than helping people judge.
pre-suasion-ch10/q01: The voucher creates a genuine give-before-ask sequence, so reciprocity fits. Tool limits and coordinator role may exist, but they are not the main cue.
pre-suasion-ch10/q02: Authority fits because the trial role answers why this speaker should discuss the protocol. General impressiveness or silencing questions would misuse the shortcut.
pre-suasion-ch10/q03: Real scarcity rests on an actual constraint. Lamination and stronger wording only change presentation, not whether the shortage is true.
pre-suasion-ch10/q04: The marked performance activates consistency with a standard singers already chose. The room’s size and the director’s warmth are not the active principle.
pre-suasion-ch10/q05: Social proof is clean when participation is real. Inflated maps or hidden rebate details pressure decisions by distorting evidence.
pre-suasion-ch10/q06: Specific observed taste makes liking credible. A smile can be empty, and changing the rule is not what makes the principle honest.
pre-suasion-ch10/q07: Principle stacking feels like pressure when the cues do not all belong. The skill is choosing the one honest route, not loading the request with every possible lever.
pre-suasion-ch10/q08: Authority fits if expert review is the true reason. Popularity and scarcity would be mismatched shortcuts if they do not explain the rule.
pre-suasion-ch10/q09: The right first question is fit. Speed and stealth turn the principles into tricks, while a truthful match keeps the setup defensible.
pre-suasion-ch11/q01: The street creates a We relationship based on shared place. Warmth and fragility may matter, but they are not the central mechanism.
pre-suasion-ch11/q02: The place cue frames the ask as service to one’s own county. It does not remove hard shifts or solve logistics.
pre-suasion-ch11/q03: The mark brings shared inheritance to consciousness. It does not answer affordability, and distraction would avoid the decision rather than prepare it.
pre-suasion-ch11/q04: Unity is clean when the identity cue is real and the request remains transparent. Device size and praise do not protect consent.
pre-suasion-ch11/q05: The doorway raises shared place identity. It does not establish ability to give, and repair details still have to be clear.
pre-suasion-ch11/q06: Shared journey can create unity, but sensitive intake requires care. Hiding the map or skipping documents misses the ethical issue.
pre-suasion-ch11/q07: False We language exploits unity. Family cues can be legitimate in some contexts, but not when used to cover a one-sided demand.
pre-suasion-ch11/q08: The shared block is a legitimate place cue. Friendliness is not unity, and prizes use a different principle.
pre-suasion-ch11/q09: The distinction is shared identity. Unity may include liking, but it goes deeper than warmth and is not automatically unethical.
pre-suasion-ch12/q01: The cadence creates togetherness around the same action the rule protects. Fatigue and rule softness are not the mechanism.
pre-suasion-ch12/q02: The shared inspection creates We before the overtime ask. Scarcity and authority may be present, but the active move is acting together.
pre-suasion-ch12/q03: The breathing action relates to the support needed in pair practice. Color and pressure would miss the unity mechanism.
pre-suasion-ch12/q04: The shared first cleanup creates practical togetherness around the equipment. Blame and elimination of maintenance are not the point.
pre-suasion-ch12/q05: Sorting creates a joint repair frame before feedback. The goal is not forgetting anger or controlling answers; it is changing the relationship honestly.
pre-suasion-ch12/q06: Shared action prepares support, but it cannot replace clear terms. Seeing color and multiple participants are part of the legitimate action.
pre-suasion-ch12/q07: Unitary activity needs fit. A chant may create motion together, but if it does not mirror the needed support, it feels like theater.
pre-suasion-ch12/q08: Doing one piece of cleanup together creates a We tied to the ask. Speeches name unity without making it, and discounts use a different road.
pre-suasion-ch12/q09: Fit to the later cooperation is the test. Humor or duration can help or hurt, but neither defines acting-together unity.
pre-suasion-ch13/q01: The ethical decision belongs before copy optimization. Legal visibility may matter, but trust cost asks whether the tactic should exist at all.
pre-suasion-ch13/q02: The ethical check asks what the fear cue does to patients and trust. Clicks and competitor behavior can reward exploitation.
pre-suasion-ch13/q03: The problem is who the cue targets and when. Polish and color are secondary if the design captures child impulse before informed choice.
pre-suasion-ch13/q04: Consent and need specificity control ethical use. Shock alone can turn suffering into a lever, and cropping may not fix missing permission or vague purpose.
pre-suasion-ch13/q05: The tester’s reaction shows a coercion risk. Hiding the erase icon would deepen the problem, and one test does not condemn every program.
pre-suasion-ch13/q06: The frame pushes comfort while removing cost from view, so the choice is not informed. Optional status does not fix hidden payment information.
pre-suasion-ch13/q07: The challenge goes beyond minimum compliance without rejecting profit itself. Ethical pre-suasion asks whether the setup can survive daylight.
pre-suasion-ch13/q08: Urgency is defensible when it accurately reflects the need and use. Speed alone is not an ethical standard.
pre-suasion-ch13/q09: The audit puts ethics before optimization. Design and process details matter later, but they do not answer whether the cue should be used.
pre-suasion-ch14/q01: The quote calendar turns the fresh yes into a next action while the reason is visible. Later email and general reflection let the attention shift cool.
pre-suasion-ch14/q02: The swap card creates an immediate procedure for tomorrow. A brochure and motivation comment do not attach the decision to a specific first behavior.
pre-suasion-ch14/q03: Choosing label wording anchors the pledge in a visible future artifact. Warm thanks are good manners, but they do not create the same follow-through procedure.
pre-suasion-ch14/q04: The calendar block attaches practice to the fresh win. Praise alone fades, and a large plan without a real slot may never happen.
pre-suasion-ch14/q05: The first correct repetition makes the new behavior physical before people leave. Larger signs and later reminders rely on attention returning by itself.
pre-suasion-ch14/q06: The repeat plus stand-light cue converts excitement into a trigger and action. Pride and equipment may help, but they do not create the first procedure.
pre-suasion-ch14/q07: The yes is fragile without a next action. Celebration is not the problem by itself; the missing procedure is.
pre-suasion-ch14/q08: Scheduling the first shift while enthusiasm is present protects the aftereffect. Later links and verbal confidence depend on motivation lasting unaided.
pre-suasion-ch14/q09: The procedure should support the person’s fresh decision, not trap or mislead them. Durability built on concealment is another ethical problem.
